paper_title: One Tokenizer To Rule Them All Emergent Language Plasticity via   Multilingual Tokenizers
caption: : Effect of vocabulary size.
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the effect of vocabulary size on accuracy (%) for two tokenization methods—universal and cluster—across three different vocabulary sizes: 100k, 175k, and 250k. The x-axis represents the vocabulary size in thousands, with values at 100k, 175k, and 250k, while the y-axis represents accuracy in percentage, ranging from 40.5% to 42.0%. The "universal" tokenizer, indicated by a blue line with star markers, shows a steady increase in accuracy from 40.5% at 100k to 41.6% at 175k, and further to 41.9% at 250k. In contrast, the "cluster" tokenizer, represented by an orange line with circle markers, starts at 41.6% at 100k, rises to 41.7% at 175k, and then declines to 41.5% at 250k. The plot demonstrates that the universal tokenizer consistently improves with larger vocabulary sizes, while the cluster tokenizer peaks at 175k and then decreases.
